The opening is a sustained pun. The "student at the University of Hong Kong" and the "courses" she must choose are not real university classes; the wordplay turns the setting into a meal. In reality, the student chose dishes—meal courses—at a restaurant or dining place. The "deadline" for choosing was the mealtime/ordering context, not an HKU enrollment deadline. She ate the meal, so by the end of the evening her plates were empty: all of the courses were gone because they had been eaten. The apparent mystery of the university student losing every enrolled class is resolved by rereading "courses" as dishes and her act of eating as what made them disappear.

The story is a wordplay puzzle built on two meanings of "courses." The student and the University of Hong Kong setting are a decoy: the real situation is a meal, and the "courses" are dishes served at a restaurant or dining place. The "deadline" is the mealtime/ordering cutoff, and "choose my courses" means selecting dishes, not registering for classes. That evening the student ate the meal, so by the end the dishes were gone—the meal courses had been consumed and the plates were empty. The apparent tragedy of an HKU student losing all her enrolled classes is resolved by rereading "courses" as dishes and "were gone" as finished or eaten.
